Neural, vascular, motor and autonomic habituation to high-intensity auditory stimulation: A multimodal characterization of the human defensive responses.
papers.abstract: The defense reflex has been extensively characterized across sensory modalities; however, the integration of electrical, neurovascular, motor, and peripheral autonomic responses involving the central and autonomic nervous systems remains poorly understood. This study investigated defensive responses to high-intensity auditory stimulation using a multimodal approach combining electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and peripheral physiological measures. Participants were exposed to twenty white-noise bursts (100 dB, 500 ms, instantaneous rise time) separated by silent intervals (50 ± 10 s), grouped into five blocks to assess initial responses and habituation. Hemodynamic responses revealed widespread activation of bilateral auditory and frontal regions following stimulus onset, with a progressive reduction in response amplitude and extension of active channels across blocks. Network analysis suggests progressive reorganization of functional connectivity between sensory and frontal regions across repeated stimulation. At the peripheral level, habituation was observed in phasic electrodermal activity, vascular indices, motor response, EEG-derived ocular activity, and parasympathetic cardiac modulation, primarily after the first block, whereas respiratory measures remained stable. Cardiac defense-like responses show a multi-temporal component structure, with habituation restricted to the late decelerative phase. Multivariate analyses revealed a structured yet partially independent organization of neural and autonomic responses to habituation. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive characterization of multisystem responses to intense auditory stimulation, highlighting selective habituation across central, neurovascular, motor, and autonomic systems, and offering new insights into how neurovascular and peripheral processes adapt to repeated auditory threats.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

papers.title: SCN2B Drives Depression-like Phenotypes in Mice by Suppressing BDNF Signaling via Its Intracellular Domain NICD.
papers.abstract: The rising global burden of depression necessitates novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets. Voltage-gated sodium channel β2-subunit (Navβ2, coded by SCN2B) has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, yet its role in depression remains unexplored. Here, we identify SCN2B as a previously unrecognized driver of depression-like pathophysiology. Using SCN2B-overexpressing (SCN2B-OV) mice across different ages (1, 12, and 20 months) and CRISPR- engineered Navβ2V173A,V175K mice with selective reduction of the Navβ2 intracellular domain (NICD), we combined behavioral phenotyping, electrophysiology, neurotransmitter profiling, and molecular analyses, with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) as an environmental challenge. SCN2B-OV mice exhibited accelerated depression-like phenotypes, including anhedonia (sucrose preference 52.42% reduction, P<0.05), behavioral despair (forced swim test immobility 67.42% increase, P<0.05), and cognitive deficits (Y-maze alternation 50.90% reduction, P<0.05), independent of natural aging. Electrophysiologically, SCN2B overexpression induced a striking prefrontal-hippocampal imbalance: prefrontal cortex (PFC) became hyperexcitable (glutamate release increased by 64.7%; sEPSC amplitude increased 2.05-fold, P<0.05), whereas the hippocampus showed synaptic suppression (GABA release reduced by 32.65%; sIPSC frequency reduced by 66.67%, P<0.05). Mechanistically, SCN2B overexpression suppressed BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling axis (BDNF reduced by 53.17%; p-TrkB reduced by 63.62%, P<0.05), accompanied by decreased synaptic proteins (PSD95 43.45%, synapsin I 40.31%, P<0.05). Remarkably, NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice were fully resistant to CUMS-induced behavioral and neurotransmitter deficits, establishing NICD as a critical mediator of stress vulnerability. Collectively, these findings unravel a causal pathway in which SCN2B overexpression drives NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF signaling, leading to region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, synaptic disintegration, and depression-like phenotypes. Targeting Navβ2 proteolysis to block NICD generation may thus represent a novel therapeutic strategy for mood disorders.

papers.title: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
papers.abstract: Efficient visual attention is fundamental to environmental adaptation and social interaction. While previous studies have observed alterations in visual processing among deaf individuals, findings remain controversial regarding whether these changes stem from hearing loss (sensory compensation vs. cognitive deficit) or sign language experience. To address this issue, the present study provides task-related and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) evidence to disentangle the specific drivers of visual selective attention plasticity. A visual search task was used to examine selective attention in 95 participants (34 prelingual deaf, 27 hearing signers, and 34 hearing nonsigners). Compared to both hearing groups, deaf individuals exhibited significantly lower hit rates and diminished N2-posterior contralateral (N2pc) amplitudes. Hearing signers and nonsigners showed comparable behavioral performance, N2pc amplitudes, and resting-state network topology, whereas the deaf group was further characterized by a degraded resting-state alpha network topology, evidenced by reduced clustering coefficients, global efficiency, and weakened frontal-occipital connectivity. N2pc amplitude correlated significantly with resting-state network properties and behavioral accuracy. These results suggest that deaf individuals may suffer from an imbalance in the regulation of visual selective attention, most clearly indexed by the evoked N2pc and by intrinsic alpha-network organization, and likely linked to increased resource competition following the loss of auditory monitoring. Our findings provide neurophysiological evidence that these attentional deficits are associated with hearing loss rather than with sign-language experience, offering a new perspective for understanding the boundaries of cross-modal plasticity in the human brain.

papers.title: EEG monitoring in the neonate as part of a multimodal brain protection system in paediatric anaesthesia.
papers.abstract: Neurological monitoring is well established in anesthesia. Applied for assessment and control it also provides indirect information on hemodynamic status, ventilation, oxygenation and perfusion. In pediatric anesthesia, the potential toxicity of anesthetics is a concern. In neonates and young infants, the brain is immature and still developing, making electroencephalogram monitoring complex. To determine the current state of neurological function monitoring in neonates during anesthesia as a brain protection tool, a narrative review was conducted. The search prioritized the last ten years in PubMed, Cochrane, other electronic sources, and snowball sampling using the keywords: Neurotoxicity, Brain Monitoring, Newborn, Anesthesia, Neuroprotective Strategies, combinations thereof, and expert publications. The review concludes that brain protection is necessary, however further knowledge and validated technological support are required.
papers.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion

papers.title: Associations of multiple ambient air pollutants and sleep apnea, sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation in adult patients with or without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects an estimated 936 million adults worldwide, yet how environmental exposures relate to sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective polysomnography-based study of 4049 adults in Shenzhen, China, to examine the relationships of ambient air pollutants, PM2.5 inorganic components, and meteorological factors with OSA severity, sleep architecture, and nocturnal oxygenation. Lag 0-180 days was selected post hoc as the main reporting window. Within this window, PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, and diurnal temperature range (DTR) were all linked to greater OSA severity. Multiple pollutants were associated with lighter sleep; for example, PM2.5 and PM10 were associated with 1.71%TST and 1.32%TST increases in N1 sleep and 1.51%TST and 1.32%TST decreases in N3 sleep, respectively. O3 and DTR showed the clearest adverse relationships with nocturnal oxygenation and sleep continuity. Non-linear analyses showed increasing exposure-response associations for PM2.5, SO2, and DTR, but a U-shaped association for O3. Interaction and mixture analyses further indicated meteorological modification and more consistent mixture relationships with altered sleep architecture than with categorical OSA severity. These findings highlight the importance of broader polysomnographic dimensions, cumulative exposure windows, and co-exposure patterns in future research.

papers.title: Charitable giving with earned and windfall money: behavioral and ERP responses to donation-risk information.
papers.abstract: Charitable giving depends both on how money is acquired and on expectations about its eventual use. However, it remains unclear how monetary source shapes the evaluation of donation-risk information after a donation decision. Twenty-six participants made repeated donation decisions using earned and windfall money while electroencephalography was recorded. After each choice, a cue indicated a 70 % probability of allocation to either a lower-credibility charity (high risk) or a higher-credibility charity (low risk). One decision and its associated allocation rule were implemented at the end of the experiment. Participants donated more from windfall than earned money and reported greater regret and lower satisfaction after high-risk than low-risk cues. Mixed-effects analysis also showed lower next-trial donations following high-risk cues. Windfall money was associated with less positive frontocentral mean voltage within the feedback-related negativity (FRN) interval, whereas low-risk information elicited a larger P3. The predicted monetary-source-by-risk interaction was not supported, and Bayesian comparisons favored the zero-interaction model over the specified alternative. These findings show that monetary acquisition context and prospective allocation information both matter for charitable giving and its neural evaluation. They extend research on donation-related feedback by demonstrating behavioral adjustment to consequential risk information before the recipient and the realized charitable outcome are known.

papers.title: Parent- and teen-reported prevalence of sleep health and habits and teen-reported associations with screen time.
papers.abstract: Nationally representative teen-reported data to examine determinants of adolescent sleep health is scarce. The current study seeks to 1) estimate the prevalence of sleep health in a national survey of teenagers, 2) explore the association between number of hours of daily screen time use and sleep health, and 3) compare differences in sleep health between teen and parent report among teen-parent pairs. Data come from the teen-reported July 2021-December 2023 National Health Interview Survey-Teen (NHIS-Teen) and the parent-reported 2022 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). The prevalence and associations between differing levels of daily screen time use (two or less hours, three hours, four hours or more) and sleep health were calculated using teen self-report. The prevalence of teen- and parent-reported sleep health and habits were estimated and compared. As daily screen time increased, the prevalence of teens reporting difficulty getting out of bed, complaining about being tired, taking naps or falling asleep during the day, and not waking up well-rested increased. Teenagers with four or more hours of daily screen time were more likely to report not having a regular bedtime or waketime when compared to teens with less daily screen time. Parents were consistently less likely to report poorer sleep health and habits than their teenagers. Findings suggest many teenagers who experience poorer sleep health also have high levels of daily screen time with a notable graded association by screen time. Parent-reported estimates of sleep health and habits were lower than teen reported estimates.

papers.title: Community-engaged protocol for the modified B-SWELL program randomized control pilot trial.
papers.abstract: Midlife Black women experience disproportionately high rates of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Evidence supports the use of culturally tailored interventions and community engagement to reduce health disparities in this population. In response, the Midlife Black Women's Stress Reduction and Wellness program (B-SWELL) was co-developed with midlife Black women to address cardiovascular risks and promote healthier lifestyle behaviors. This study aims to: (1) Refine the B-SWELL program to enhance sustainability, update outcome metrics in alignment with American Heart Association guidelines, and integrate findings from a prior feasibility trial; and (2) Conduct a randomized controlled pilot trial of the modified B-SWELL program to assess trends in primary and secondary outcomes and explore the preferences of midlife Black women participating in clinical research. Program refinements were guided by a community-engaged approach. The randomized controlled pilot trial compares the modified B-SWELL intervention with an attention control condition. Midlife Black women from the community will be recruited for participation. The primary outcome is cardiovascular health; secondary outcomes include depressive symptoms, unhealthy days, sleep quality, perceived general health, and symptom burden. Objectives 1 and 2 have been completed. Although the final sample did not reach the target of 64 participants, five cohorts, each comprised of an intervention group and an attention control group, completed the trial with only 9% attrition. The B-SWELL modifications highlight the value of culturally tailored, community-engaged approaches in addressing persistent cardiovascular health disparities among midlife Black women. Clinicaltrials.gov Registration Number: NCT06707636.

papers.title: Neuroinformatics in Pakistan: building a national framework for data-driven Neuroscience and Neurotechnology.
papers.abstract: Neuroinformatics represents a rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field that integrates Neuroscience, computational science, artificial intelligence, and data engineering to acquire, manage, analyze, and interpret increasingly complex brain data. Advances in Neuroimaging, electrophysiology, multimodal data integration, and computational Neuroscience have made robust Neuroinformatics infrastructure essential for modern data-driven Neuroscience, precision medicine, and intelligent clinical decision support. This Perspective examines the emerging Neuroinformatics landscape in Pakistan, examining institutional research capacity, computational infrastructure, educational and training initiatives, funding mechanisms, clinical informatics, and emerging Neurotechnology and industrial activities. Global developments in Neuroinformatics and Neurotechnology are also examined to contextualize Pakistan's current position and identify opportunities for strategic integration into the international Neuroscience ecosystem. Major barriers are critically evaluated, including fragmented neurological data resources, limited high-performance computing capacity, shortages of interdisciplinary expertise, regulatory and ethical challenges, inadequate interoperability, and barriers to sustained academic-clinical-industrial collaboration. Building on this evidence-informed assessment, this Perspective proposes a national strategy centered on interoperable Neurodata repositories, shared computational infrastructure, interdisciplinary workforce development, responsible data governance, strengthened research-industry partnerships, and international collaboration. Collectively, these priorities provide a practical roadmap for transforming existing computational and Neuroscience capabilities into a coordinated national Neuroinformatics ecosystem. Strategic investment in these areas could strengthen neurological research, accelerate data-driven clinical innovation, and position Pakistan as a more active contributor to the global Neuroinformatics and Neurotechnology landscape.

papers.title: Rest-activity rhythm robustness and prospective mood symptoms in adolescence: Moderating effects of chronotype, sleep timing, and reward sensitivity.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period of heightened bipolar spectrum disorder (BSD) risk involving changes in reward and circadian systems. Circadian disruptions can destabilize mood, and the impact may be more pronounced in individuals with trait vulnerabilities. We tested whether greater reward sensitivity or eveningness influenced the predictive association between rest-activity rhythm (RAR) disruption and dimensional mood symptoms relevant to BSD. Adolescents (N = 199) in a prospective BSD-risk study completed baseline measures of reward sensitivity, morningness-eveningness, mood symptoms, and one week of actigraphy to generate Circadian Function Index (CFI), a composite measure of RAR robustness. Mood measures were readministered six months later. Regression models tested interactions between reward sensitivity, morningness-eveningness, and sleep midpoint and CFI to predict hypo-/manic or depressive symptom severity at follow-up. CFI was not independently associated with mood symptoms. Morningness-eveningness (b = 0.59, p < .001) and sleep midpoint (b = -2.77, p = .013) significantly moderated the association between CFI and hypo-/manic symptoms. Sleep midpoint (b = -5.40, p = .023) and reward sensitivity (b = -1.32, p = .033) significantly moderated the association between CFI and depressive symptoms. The impact of CFI on mood symptoms depended upon vulnerabilities. Lower CFI predicted greater hypo-/manic symptoms among adolescents with greater eveningness and later sleep midpoint. Lower CFI predicted greater depressive symptoms among those with later sleep midpoint. Contrary to hypotheses, higher CFI predicted greater depressive symptoms for adolescents with reward hyposensitivity. These results highlight potential targets for future identification studies relevant to BSD.

papers.title: What can we learn from patients about early warning signs of (hypo)mania?
papers.abstract: To improve self-management in bipolar disorders (BD), it is essential to refine the characterisation of early warning signs (EWS) of (hypo)mania from patients' perspective. In crisis plans, patients describe EWS based on their personal experience, including signs that are primarily internally noticeable. Investigate how patients describe EWS of (hypo)mania, by qualitative analysis of their crisis plans. EWS and later signs of (hypo)mania from crisis plans were extracted and analysed through qualitative directed content analysis. The crisis plans were created by adult patients from a specialised outpatient clinic for BD, with support of relatives and a trained nurse as part of standard care. Crisis plans of 383 patients, containing 6510 signs of (hypo)mania, were coded into the following ten main categories: emotions, thought process, self-reflection, thought content, cognitive functioning, physical signs, sleep, behaviour, communication process, and communication reciprocity. Patients reported a broad spectrum of EWS, including signs that do not overlap with BD classification criteria such as suspiciousness, changed sense of time, increased sensibility to stimuli and control-seeking behaviour. They also reflected on changed insight in EWS during early (hypo)mania. Internally noticeable signs were most pronounced in later phases of (hypo)mania. Crisis plans are cocreated by patients, their relatives and mental healthcare professionals, as partly reflected by the use of medical language in the wording of the signs. EWS of (hypo)mania constitute a broad spectrum of signs, many of which are internally noticeable and not captured by BD classification criteria.
authors: Kees C W M de Schepper

papers.title: Altered Neural Oscillatory Coupling Reveals Cognitive Control Deficits with Hierarchical Characteristics and Emotional Specificity in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Cognitive control deficits are a prevalent feature of major depressive disorder (MDD) and are influenced by emotional contexts. However, it remains unclear whether these deficits specifically exist at particular hierarchical levels of cognitive control and whether they are selectively exacerbated under distinct emotional contexts. Furthermore, the neural mechanisms underlying such deficits and their association with depressive symptoms remain to be further elucidated. To fill these gaps, two experiments were conducted. In Experiment 1, 54 MDDs and 41 healthy controls (HCs) performed emotional and non-emotional hierarchical cognitive control tasks. Hierarchical demands were manipulated using low- and high-abstraction rules. Based on hierarchy- and emotion-specific deficits identified in Experiment 1, Experiment 2 (34 MDDs; 28 HCs) introduced rule memory set-size manipulation to test whether the deficit generalized to other hierarchical cognitive control subprocesses. Electroencephalography and eye-tracking were simultaneously recorded. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) quantified cross-frequency interactions subserving cognitive control. Delta-beta PAC was selectively reduced in MDDs compared with HCs during high-abstraction conditions under negative emotional contexts, but not in low-abstraction conditions or other contexts. Under the same conditions, MDDs also failed to show the typical memory-related increase in theta-gamma PAC. Moreover, emotion regulation scores significantly mediated the pathway from PAC abnormalities to depressive severity. Our findings indicate that altered neural oscillatory coupling reveals cognitive control deficits in MDD that exhibit both hierarchical characteristics and emotional specificity. These neural abnormalities may contribute to depressive severity through maladaptive emotion regulation strategies, providing a novel biological account of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying MDD.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

papers.title: Longitudinal associations among psychophysical factors, biobehavioral vulnerabilities and pain-related outcomes following acute musculoskeletal injury in adolescents.
papers.abstract: Up to 30% of adolescents with acute musculoskeletal (MSK) injuries develop chronic pain. Research has increasingly focused on identification of risk factors associated with outcomes following acute injury; however, prospective longitudinal studies examining both psychophysical and biobehavioral factors beyond short-term follow-up are limited in adolescents. The current study used mixed effects models (MEM) to test longitudinal associations among biobehavioral factors (e.g., sleep disturbances, anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-related cognitions and behaviors), psychophysical responses (e.g., conditioned pain modulation, temporal summation) and pain-related outcomes (pain intensity, pain-related disability and quality of life; QOL) over one year following acute MSK injury. Participants were 226 adolescents 11-17 years (and one parent) participating in a prospective longitudinal study with data collected via self-report, actigraphy and quantitative sensory testing (QST) at three timepoints (< 30 days, 3 months, 12 months post-injury). Results of MEM revealed within and between-person associations among psychological factors and pain-related disability and QOL. Sleep duration (within-person effect) and pain-related cognitions and behaviors (between-person effect) were associated with pain intensity. Pain-related cognitions and behaviors were also associated with pain-related disability (between-person effect) and QOL (within and between-person effects). Temporal summation (TS) was the only psychophysical factor associated with pain outcomes (between-person effect) with higher average TS associated with higher pain intensity. Findings point to the relatively stronger influence of biobehavioral (versus psychophysical) factors as responsive indicators of adolescents' recovery trajectories and suggest targeted interventions may be directed at general anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-specific cognitions and behaviors, and sleep to improve outcomes. PERSPECTIVE: This article presents results of a longitudinal multi-method study examining pain-related outcomes in adolescents following musculoskeletal injury. Findings point to the influence of biobehavioral factors in the longer-term recovery period and suggest potential importance of interventions targeting general anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-specific cognitions and behaviors, and sleep in adolescents post musculoskeletal injury.

papers.title: Elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances semantic organization and long-term memory.
papers.abstract: One longstanding goal in psychology is to identify more effective ways of learning. Recent work has shown that elaborative processing can amplify the memory benefits of retrieval practice, yet the mechanisms underlying this advantage remain unclear. Using electroencephalography (EEG), the present study examined how elaborative processing before retrieval practice influences later memory and encoding-related neural processing and representations, relative to context processing. Behaviorally, memory performance was better for elaborative processing plus retrieval practice than for context processing plus retrieval practice. During the first encoding phase, elaborative processing elicited a more negative N400, whereas context processing elicited a more positive LPC. Moreover, the N400 and LPC differences between elaborative and context processing during encoding were significantly correlated with the corresponding differences in 7-day recognition performance. Representational similarity analyses further showed stronger semantic-category organization and greater representational reorganization across repeated encoding under elaborative processing than under context processing. These findings suggest that elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances long-term memory and is associated with broader semantic processing and stronger semantic organization during encoding. More broadly, the results suggest that richer connections with pre-existing semantic knowledge may be one way in which encoding variability supports long-term memory.

papers.title: Chinese Ethnic Traditional Sports as Mind-Body Interventions for Psychiatric Recovery.
papers.abstract: Chinese ethnic traditional sports (CETS)-a family of culturally embedded physical practices encompassing traditional Chinese mind-body exercises (e.g., Tai Chi, Qigong, Baduanjin, Yijin Jing, Wuqinxi) and intangible cultural heritage folk sports (e.g., dragon-lion dance)-have attracted growing interest as accessible, low-cost mind-body interventions for mental health. This narrative review examines which mental health outcomes are associated with participation in different types of CETS and to what extent the available evidence supports their role in psychiatric recovery. The review synthesizes 68 studies published between January 2000 and June 2026, identified through multi-database searches of Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus. Thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions of mental health burden addressed by CETS: (a) affective disorders; (b) trauma-related disorders; (c) sleep-wake disturbances; and (d) cognitive and psychosocial dysfunction. Across these dimensions, individual randomized controlled trials consistently report moderate reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms, with larger effects when CETS are delivered in supervised groups at moderate intensity for 12-24 weeks; however, most evidence derives from subclinical or non-psychiatric samples and measures symptom severity rather than functional recovery. The review therefore concludes that CETS are a promising, low-cost, culturally congruent adjunct to conventional psychiatric care-warranting rigorous, disorder-specific trials-rather than established stand-alone treatments for psychiatric recovery.

papers.title: Extending the Structured Days Hypothesis to Children With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities: A Conceptual Framework.
papers.abstract: The Structured Days Hypothesis suggests that the school day helps to regulate obesogenic behaviors, whereas out-of-school periods (e.g., summer) contribute to worsening obesogenic behaviors (e.g., low levels of physical activity, increased screen time, later sleep patterns, and unhealthy diet). However, little is known about how out-of-school periods impact children with intellectual and developmental disabilities who experience diagnosis-related challenges and unique family circumstances. This paper outlines a conceptual framework that proposes how out-of-school periods may be associated with obesogenic behaviors in children with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and how child- and family-level factors moderate this relationship. The hypotheses generated from the extension of the Structured Days Hypothesis to children will guide future research in this area, providing insight into who and when the risk for worsening obesogenic behavior is the greatest. This future research will provide information to help inform policies and interventions aimed at improving health outcomes and increasing access to supportive environments for this population.

papers.title: Comprehensive assessment of prediction of pH in red meat based on near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS).
papers.abstract: pH is an indicator of meat quality, affecting colour, tenderness, and shelf life. This study is aimed to carry a comprehensive assessment of non-invasive prediction model for pH using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) across red meat species. A calibration model based on 2539 samples was built using a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN), integrating data from 17 muscles, 3 species (beef, lamb, venison), and 4 NIRS devices. The model achieved a strong calibration performance (R2 = 0.95, SEP = 0.07) and a competent validation performance (R2 = 0.82, SEP = 0.14). External testing confirmed the model's ability to predict pH across different animals and muscles, although reduced accuracy was observed with the INDIGO handheld device. The lack of ability to capture information related to muscle structure reduced the prediction performance of the sensor and generated bias. Results confirm the feasibility of a robust NIRS-based tool for meat pH assessment, provided device used to collect NIR spectra is suitable for red meat. This approach opens new opportunities for real-time quality control in meat processing, with a potential to improve consistency and reduce losses due to pH-related defects.

papers.title: Comment on "Prevalence and clinical associations of sleep-disordered breathing in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis".
Is Mg2+ sensed by adenylate kinase and serving as a signal of energy status in biological systems? (a hypothesis).
papers.abstract: The contents of adenylates and free magnesium (Mg2+) are controlled by adenylate kinase (AK), which equilibrates specific Mg-bound and free adenylates. Taking into account the true substrates of AK, the reaction is described as: MgATP + AMPfree ↔ MgADP + ADPfree, and its equilibrium constant (K) does not depend on [Mg2+]. However, when the reaction is described in terms of total contents of adenylates, i.e., ATPtot + AMPtot ↔ 2 ADPtot, its apparent K (Kapp) varies from 0.3 to 1.5, depending on [Mg2+]. Here, we argue that Mg2+ is sensed by AK via the availability of its apparent substrates (total adenylates), and that changes in its Kapp affect internal [Mg2+]; the higher the Kapp (and energy status), the lower the [Mg2+], and vice versa. In this way, Mg2+ becomes a signal of true cellular energy charge. The Mg2+-signal controls myriad metabolic and developmental processes, including kinase reactions, photosynthesis, respiration, circadian rhythms, etc., integrating metabolism and development. The AK sensing of Mg2+ and its control over the Mg2+-signal may represent a robust and sensitive measure of energy charge. It may also be universal for any organism containing AK, with shifts in [Mg2+] as vital outputs of its activity and subsequent adenylate metabolism.

papers.title: An intelligible mathematical framework for quantifying neuro-behavioural fatigue and adaptive risk evaluation in educational settings.
papers.abstract: University students often experience multiple sources of stress, including academic, digital, and lifestyle-related factors. Traditional fatigue assessment tools are largely based on psychometric questionnaires capturing subjective evaluations of fatigue. However, such tools rarely account for multiple interrelated factors in a cohesive framework. This paper introduces the interpretable computational framework known as the Neuro-Behavioural Fatigue Assessment Model (NFAM) for identifying neuro-behavioural fatigue based on commonly reported questionnaire data. The framework employs a composite fatigue index characterized by three underlying components. The first component is the Cognitive Fatigue Index (CFI), which represents fatigue-related factors associated with attention and recovery. The second component is the Digital Overload Multiplier (DOM), which accounts for interaction effects between digital activity and academic engagement. The third component is the Sleep Efficiency Model (SEM), which estimates the sleep-related contribution to overall fatigue using lifestyle factors. The components were combined to form the composite score (i.e., the NFAM composite). The framework was evaluated using the data from 1000 university students. Preliminary assessment of the questionnaire variables suggested that the NFAM is better conceptualised as a formative computational framework rather than a reflective psychometric instrument. The sensitivity analysis of the weightings indicated that the framework remained stable under alternative weighting configurations. The statistical analysis indicated significant differences between the defined fatigue-risk categories, consistent framework performance across the evaluated participants, and the ability to explain individual responses using the composite index. Overall, the current study provides an interpretable framework for assessing neuro-behavioural fatigue in a university student population. Future research will include external validation of the NFAM using independent datasets and established psychometric fatigue measures.

papers.title: EEG network analysis to identify cortical pathology in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify preoperative electrophysiologic biomarkers to localize the epileptogenic zone (EZ) and predict surgical outcomes in patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) using a graph-theoretical network analysis. We retrospectively analyzed preoperative long-term EEG data from 71 LGS patients in three subgroups: Group A (n = 23), with favorable outcomes after resective surgery (RS); Group B (n = 22), with unfavorable outcomes after RS; and Group C (n = 26), who underwent palliative surgery instead of RS. We analyzed 500-ms EEG windows centered on the point of peak phase coupling preceding interictal generalized sharp-and-slow waves. We computed two sets of biomarkers: (1) the clustering coefficient (CCE) to assess overall network connectivity, and (2) a novel 'Network Dominance Score' (the product of Betweenness Centrality, Node Out-Degree, and Node Out-Strength) to identify the putative ictogenic hub. The CCE effectively differentiate the favorable-outcome group (Group A), the unfavorable-outcome group (Group B), and the palliative surgery group (Group C) (Area Under the Curve = 0.915). The Network Dominance Score achieved 100% accuracy in correctly lateralizing the lesion for all patients in the Group A. Conversely, for the Group B, this analysis identified either bilateral or incorrectly localized hubs, demonstrating a clear correlation between our analytical findings and surgical outcomes. This graph-theoretical approach offers a promising non-invasive tool to augment conventional presurgical evaluations, improve patient selection for RS, and predict surgical outcomes in individuals with LGS.

papers.title: Clinical meaning of significant intraindividual asymmetries in material-specific memory performance within the unimpaired range in 432 people with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Material-specific memory deficits can provide lateralizing information regarding epileptogenic foci or structural lesions. Intraindividual performance asymmetries may occur despite overall unimpaired performance. This study investigates the clinical relevance of such asymmetries in people with epilepsy (PWE). We retrospectively analyzed data from 432 PWE who demonstrated unimpaired verbal and figural memory performance but exhibited significant intraindividual asymmetries in these domains, as determined by critical differences derived from co-normed data. Concordance between material-specific memory asymmetries and lateralization from MRI and EEG lateralization was evaluated using contingency tables and chi-square/Fisher's exact tests. Among 1,246 individuals with suspected epilepsy and unimpaired memory performance, 432 (34.7 %) with confirmed epilepsy diagnosis exhibited significant material-specific asymmetries. Of these, 367 (85.0 %) demonstrated a relative verbal memory superiority, and 65 (15.0 %) showed a figural memory superiority. Among PWE with lateralized temporal pathologies, Fisher's exact test showed a significant association between memory asymmetries and MRI lateralization, p = .036, V = .167. A chi-square test demonstrated no significant association between memory asymmetries and EEG lateralization, χ²(1) = 3.57, p = .059. No significant concordance emerged when temporal MRI and EEG findings were considered jointly, χ2(1) = 3.54, p = .060. The majority of PWE with significant intraindividual material-specific memory asymmetries within the unimpaired range exhibit verbal memory superiority. There is a statistically significant association of this performance asymmetry with MRI lateralization. In case of temporal pathologies, memory asymmetries clearly point to lateralized MRI pathologies, although the actual side cannot be reliably predicted due to putative reorganization processes.

papers.title: Interictal epileptic discharge > 1% associated with cognitive impairment in adult patients with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study based on dose-response relationship and discharge characteristics.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is frequently accompanied by multidomain cognitive impairment, but the quantitative contribution of interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs)-including discharge burden, vigilance state, and spatial distribution-to specific cognitive domains remains incompletely defined. This cross-sectional study aimed to examine associations between multidimensional IED parameters and domain-specific cognitive function in non-symptomatic adult epilepsy. We analyzed long-term EEG-derived IED indices during sleep and wakefulness, lateralization, focal/multifocal distribution, and frontal/temporal involvement in 114 adults with non-symptomatic epilepsy, relating these metrics to a neuropsychological battery using ANCOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After adjustment for age, education, disease duration, seizure duration, seizure frequency, and antiepileptic drug count, a sleep IED index > 1% remained associated with lower Montreal Cognitive Assessment, associative learning, and verbal fluency scores versus the < 1% group; Mini-Mental State Examination was borderline and visual recognition did not survive FDR. Compared with no discharge, sleep > 1% showed lower Digit Symbol and verbal fluency scores only at uncorrected significance. For wakefulness, no significant graded association emerged between < 1% and > 1% groups; versus no discharge, wake > 1% showed lower Digit Symbol and verbal fluency scores at uncorrected level only. Discharges during both sleep and wakefulness were associated with lower backward digit span than sleep-only discharges, with a trend after FDR. Lateralization and focal/multifocal distribution were not significantly associated after FDR. Frontal IEDs were associated with lower verbal fluency and attention-related scores versus no discharge, but direct regional contrasts were nonsignificant and limited by small subgroups. A sleep IED index > 1% may represent a candidate electrophysiological marker of domain-specific cognitive vulnerability, whereas a wakefulness threshold and clear regional specificity were not definitively established. These findings support vigilance-state-aware quantification of IED burden while highlighting the need for larger longitudinal studies with detailed medication profiling.

papers.title: A synchronized dual-scale platform combining flexible micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG reveals frequency-dependent cortex-to-skull spectral gain in awake mice.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most scalable window onto brain dynamics, yet how cortical activity is transformed before reaching extracranial electrodes has largely been inferred from forward models rather than directly measured. We built a dual-scale sensing platform in awake mice that records a 16-channel flexible micro-electrocorticography (micro-ECoG) array and five skull-screw EEG electrodes on a single 30-kHz clock, enabling sample-aligned comparison of cortical and skull-level signals. Across 115 simultaneously recorded ECoG-EEG pairs from three mice, cortex-to-skull spectral gain was not frequency-flat but increased with frequency following a power law, indicating that skull EEG relatively preserves high-frequency cortical activity rather than acting as a simple low-pass copy. This gain was also non-stationary: it shifted across blocks of a fixed-order auditory protocol and was not explained by measured video motion, whereas trial-matched cross-scale coherence depended on the reference transform. With channel number equalized, micro-ECoG retained a larger unique spatial component than skull EEG. These results convert the cortex-to-skull relationship from a static modeling assumption into a measurable, frequency- and state-dependent quantity. For neural sensing, they provide an empirical calibration target for choosing electrode scale, reference, and analysis band and for validating EEG forward models and EEG-to-intracranial translation. More broadly, they indicate that noninvasive biomarkers and brain-computer interface features, particularly in high-frequency bands, should be interpreted through frequency- and state-aware cortex-to-skull mappings.

papers.title: Guest editorial: Adverse childhood experiences and sleep health, Why context matters!
Systematic Review of the Literature on Associations Between Symptoms, Stress, Resilience, and Epigenetic Aging in Patients With Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer and its treatments can have long-term adverse effects that may accelerate aging and worsen symptom burden. The cognitive and behavioral strategies that patients utilize to adapt to their environment and respond to stress may influence inter-individual variability in aging and symptom burden. This systematic review summarizes the relationships between symptoms, stress, resilience, and epigenetic aging in oncology patients and identifies knowledge gaps. A search of relevant databases was done from January 2000 to May 2026. Studies were included that examined DNA methylation patterns to predict biological age using algorithms known as epigenetic clocks in adults with cancer. A qualitative synthesis of the quantitative studies is reported. Of the 10 studies included in this review, a total of nine different methods were used to predict epigenetic age. The most common methods were the Levine, Horvath, and Hannum clocks. Nine studies reported on associations between symptoms and epigenetic age acceleration; one study reported on an association between stress and epigenetic age acceleration; and one study reported on an association between resilience and epigenetic age acceleration. More longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and investigate variations by epigenetic age estimate, timing of assessment, cancer type, and stage of disease. Studies are needed to evaluate the role of stress and resilience in mediating/moderating the relationships between epigenetic age acceleration and symptoms in patients with cancer. A subset of patients with cancer who develop more severe fatigue, pain, sleep disturbance, peripheral motor neuropathy, cognitive, depressive, and/or anxiety symptoms may experience epigenetic age acceleration. This systematic review was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42024545895).

papers.title: Is bedsharing beyond infancy associated with childhood and adolescent depression and anxiety?
papers.abstract: Research on bedsharing, the practice of parents sleeping on the same surface with their children, has largely focused on infancy, with little known about the implications of bedsharing that begins beyond the first year of life. To examine whether bedsharing beyond infancy is associated with an increased risk of depression and anxiety in childhood and adolescence. Participants (N = 7077) were drawn from The Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC). Mothers reported their children's nighttime sleep location at 6 months, 18 months, and 3.5 years. Diagnoses of depression and anxiety disorders were assessed at child ages 8 and 13 years. Later-onset bedsharing (at 18 months or 3.5 years, but not at 6 months) was associated with an increased likelihood of anxiety disorders at age 8 (adjusted OR = 2.83, 95% CI = 1.40-5.71), and this association remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Later-onset bedsharing was also associated with anxiety disorders at age 13 (adjusted OR = 2.84; 95% CI = 1.14-7.04), although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between early-only bedsharing (at 6 months) and depression or anxiety disorders at either age 8 or 13 years. Findings suggest that not all bedsharing is associated with later adverse outcomes. Bedsharing that begins beyond infancy may reflect different underlying child, family, or developmental factors than bedsharing occurring only in infancy and may serve as a marker of elevated risk for later anxiety.

papers.title: Synergistic inhibitory mechanism of peptide and β-glucan from oat on α-glucosidase was explored by molecular docking and spectroscopy analyses.
papers.abstract: Natural hypoglycemic active substances have attracted extensive attention. A novel hypoglycemic peptide was identified from oat bran. The <3 kDa ultrafiltration fraction of oat protein hydrolysate was identified via LC-MS/MS, and the peptide Arg-Glu-Leu-Gly-Gly-Phe-Phe (RELGGFF) was screened, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 531.90 ± 5.23 μg/mL against α-glucosidase. The synergistic α-glucosidase inhibitory effect and mechanism when combined with oat β-glucan were investigated in vitro. The combination of 800 μg/mL RELGGFF and 50 mg/mL oat β-glucan produced the strongest synergistic effect, achieving an enzyme inhibition rate of 71.14 ± 1.52% and a combination index (CI) value of 0.71. Molecular docking and spectral analysis indicated that RELGGFF and oat β-glucan could tightly bind to α-glucosidase and synergistically inhibit its activity by influencing its conformational stability. This study established a theoretical foundation for the synergistic application of RELGGFF and oat β-glucan in the management of type 2 diabetes (T2D).

papers.title: Prefrontal rTMS modulates dynamic expectancy processes to shape subsequent pain experience.
papers.abstract: Pain expectancy is a major determinant of pain perception, and identifying effective approaches to modulate expectancy may provide new opportunities for pain intervention. High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) has been implicated in expectancy-related pain modulation. However, it remains unclear how DLPFC-rTMS influences distinct stages of expectancy processing and how these changes relate to subsequent pain experience. Thirty-three healthy participants completed a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover study. Participants received real or sham high-frequency DLPFC-rTMS and performed a pain expectancy paradigm before and after stimulation while EEG was recorded. The paradigm dissociated expectancy formation and maintenance under certain and uncertain predictive contexts. Behaviorally, DLPFC-rTMS reduced pain intensity and unpleasantness, accompanied by a reduction in expected pain, and mediation analysis identified an indirect effect through expected pain. At the neural level, DLPFC-rTMS increased contextual cue-evoked P2 responses relative to sham during expectancy formation but reduced anticipatory N1 and contingent negative variation (CNV) responses during expectancy maintenance. During pain experience, laser-evoked N1 responses showed a context-dependent pattern, with greater attenuation under uncertainty. Importantly, mediation analyses identified distinct stage-related indirect associations: stimulation-related changes in contextual P2 responses were linked to subsequent laser-evoked N1 responses, whereas changes in anticipatory CNV and anxiety were jointly associated with subsequent pain ratings. Together, these findings demonstrate that DLPFC-rTMS modulates dynamic expectancy processes across distinct stages of pain anticipation, with formation- and maintenance-related changes linked to different aspects of subsequent pain processing.

papers.title: Learning discriminative time-frequency representations for EEG segment-level seizure-state classification with channel selection.
papers.abstract: AbstractElectroencephalography (EEG)-based seizure monitoring supports the diagnosis andmanagement of epilepsy; however, high-dimensional multichannel EEG recordings imposesubstantial computational burden and limit suitability for portable monitoring systems.This paper proposes a reduced-channel framework for segment-level classification of EEGinto ictal, preictal and interictal states. It integrates attention-guided EEG channelselection, high-resolution time-frequency analysis via the Time ReassignedMultiSynchroSqueezing Transform (TMSST) and Concentration of Frequency and Time(ConceFT), and a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM classifier. The framework is evaluated on theCHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG databases under two complementary protocols: astratified 70/30 holdout split and rigorous Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validationto assess subject independent generalization. Under holdout evaluation using a single EEGchannel, the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.28 ± 0.63%, sensitivity of99.18%, specificity of 99.64%, and MCC of 0.97 on CHB-MIT, and an accuracy of98.75 ± 0.74%, sensitivity of 98.77%, specificity of 99.38%, and MCC(Matthews correlationcoefficients) of 0.97 on Siena. LOSO cross-validation demonstrates subject independentgeneralization, exceeding 91% accuracy on both databases. These results demonstrate thatthe framework achieves an effective balance among segment-level classification accuracy,computational efficiency and reduced-channel operation. Moreover, applicability forportable and wearable EEG-based seizure-state monitoring applications is investigated.

papers.title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins.
papers.abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

papers.title: Individualised electrophysiological neural field models for the assessment of thalamocortical function in disorders of consciousness: A multicentre study.
papers.abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying disorders of consciousness (DoC) remains a major challenge, particularly in distinguishing limited awareness in minimally conscious state (MCS) and complete unawareness in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, also coined vegetative state (UWS/VS). In this multicentre study, we fitted a biophysically informed corticothalamic neural field model to high-density EEG data from two large independent datasets, comprising 203 UWS patients, 270 MCS patients and 74 healthy controls. We then used the fitted parameters to simulate EEG time series on a per-subject basis and compared empirical and simulated complexity metrics. The model reliably captured the spectral features across different states of consciousness and revealed reduced corticothalamic integrity in DoC patients that was more pronounced in UWS than in MCS, supporting the mesocircuit hypothesis. Furthermore, the simulated EEG reproduced the complexity patterns of the empirical recordings, with permutation entropy emerging as a sensitive marker capable of distinguishing between MCS and UWS for both real and simulated time series.

papers.title: Harnessing AI for Hypothyroidism Monitoring Using Wearable-Derived Heart Rate Data: Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Hypothyroidism is a prevalent endocrine disorder characterized by an insidious onset and nonspecific symptoms, often leading to significant diagnostic delays. While biochemical thyroid function tests (TFTs) are the gold standard, their invasive nature and cost make them impractical for continuous, proactive screening of at-risk populations. Thyroid hormones exert direct chronotropic effects on the cardiovascular system, and their levels are closely correlated with heart rate (HR). Wearable devices capable of continuous HR monitoring offer a novel opportunity for noninvasive, digital phenotype-based detection. This study aimed to develop and validate an AI-assisted system that uses wearable-derived sleep HR data as a digital monitoring tool for individuals at risk of hypothyroidism, helping identify those who warrant further confirmatory thyroid testing. This retrospective cohort study used 1677 paired observations consisting of sleep HR data and serum TFT results, including free thyroxine (T4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels, from 413 participants (mean age 43.1, SD 9.7 y; women: n=314, 76%). Participants wore consumer-grade wearables (Fitbit) that recorded HR and sleep data. Each TFT result was paired with sleep HR data extracted from the 15 consecutive nights preceding the blood test. An AI system was developed using a gradient boosting algorithm (LightGBM) to classify thyroid status by integrating baseline TFT results with statistical and temporal HR features. The model's performance was evaluated using patient-level leave-one-out cross-validation. To examine the benefit of longitudinal data, performance was compared using 1, 2, or 3 prior paired observations as reference points. To ensure clinical relevance and avoid performance inflation from hyperthyroid cases, we prioritized the analysis of a subset containing only euthyroid and hypothyroid data (n=744 paired observations). In this clinically challenging subset, the system achieved an accuracy of 74.6%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 73.5% using a single-reference data pair. Incorporating longitudinal HR patterns further enhanced performance; using 3 reference pairs improved accuracy to 78.1% (sensitivity 81.8% and specificity 77.7%). In the overall dataset (n=1677 paired observations), the system demonstrated an accuracy of 80.8%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 80.8% using a single-reference pair. Notably, the system achieved high clinical safety by detecting 96.3% of severe overt hypothyroidism cases (free T4 <0.5 ng/dL). This AI-assisted system demonstrates the feasibility of a sensitive, noninvasive longitudinal monitoring tool for hypothyroidism, robustly identifying a high proportion of hypothyroid cases-particularly severe ones-to prioritize at-risk individuals for confirmatory blood tests. Given the predominantly female iatrogenic-withdrawal cohort, prospective sex-balanced validation in primary hypothyroidism is warranted.

papers.title: Defining and measuring proximity to criticality based on univariate time series.
papers.abstract: Diverse social, engineered, and biological systems are made up of multiple interacting dynamical components; to work properly, certain components must be carefully regulated so that their dynamics avoid instability. However, many desirable properties, like optimized computation and control, emerge close to the tipping point between stability and instability, i.e., near criticality. Claims that such dynamical systems operate near criticality have been controversial because it is difficult to assess proximity to criticality when control parameters are unknown, hard to manipulate experimentally, and fluctuating in response to changing environmental or internal conditions. Moreover, observations of system dynamics are often limited to time series measurements of one or a few components. Here we develop a temporal renormalization group theory for defining criticality for univariate time series models and an information theoretic definition of proximity to criticality that is independent of model parameterization. We apply this theory to order-n autoregressive models resulting in a data-analytic strategy for time-resolved estimates of proximity to criticality based on measured univariate time series. After benchmarking our approach on diverse ground-truth cases, we apply it to recordings of spiking activity in the mammalian brain. Our estimate of proximity to criticality predicts behavior and suggests that brain dynamics shift closer to criticality during wakefulness and shift away during deep sleep.

papers.title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels.
papers.abstract: Intracellular Ca2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K+ channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K+ currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (CaV) channels that provide localized Ca2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+CaV channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β4 (BKβ4), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and CaV channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ4 promotes BK+CaV nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the CaV subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+CaV channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.
