Sleep-dependent DNA methylation remodeling in basolateral amygdala fear engrams.
papers.abstract: How sleep consolidates fear memories at the molecular level within individual engram neurons is unknown. Using activity-dependent tagging and sequencing, we profiled the DNA methylome and transcriptome of engram and non-engram nuclei from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) after contextual fear conditioning with and without post-learning sleep deprivation. Fear learning induces coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engram neurons, with each showing unique temporal dynamics, revealing CpH methylation as a separate component of the engram's epigenetic signature. Interestingly, sleep deprivation partially reverses learning-induced methylation changes and impairs memory recall, indicating that sleep supports engram-specific epigenetic consolidation. Integrating the engram methylome with single-cell transcriptome profiling, we construct a multi-omic molecular atlas of the BLA fear engram and identify Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target. BLA-wide and engram-specific Mid1 knockdown establishes its functional requirement for fear memory consolidation, providing an approach to identify behaviorally relevant epigenetic targets.

papers.title: Disrupted Top-Down Modulation as a Mechanism of Impaired Multisensory Processing in Autistic Children.
papers.abstract: Atypical sensory processing is commonly observed in autism, particularly when integration across sensory modalities is required. The neural mechanisms underlying multisensory differences remain unclear. We recorded EEG while autistic children aged 8-13 (AU;n = 40), siblings of autistic children (SIB;n = 26), and non-autistic controls (NA;n = 36) performed a simple reaction-time task to auditory (A), visual (V), and audiovisual (AV) stimuli. Analyses targeted event-related potentials (ERPs), alpha-band event-related desynchronization (α-ERD), and long-range theta-band functional connectivity. Groups did not differ across unisensory measures, indicating comparable unisensory processing. By contrast, multisensory integration (MSI;AV-(A+V)) differed across groups: NA children showed significant ERP MSI over parieto-central sites that was absent in AU and SIB; and α-ERD MSI was significantly reduced in AU, with SIB showing an intermediate profile. Connectivity analyses revealed reduced AV fronto-parieto-occipital coupling in autistic children relative to non-autistic children, suggesting weaker large-scale coordination during multisensory processing. These results point to a multisensory-specific deficit spanning early sensory encoding, posterior α-ERD, and fronto-posterior coupling and support disrupted multisensory influences on sensory processing due to reduced multisensory attentional orienting. SIB profiles suggest inherited liability for these neural phenotypes. These results help explain well-documented behavioral MSI differences in autism by linking impaired early enhancement with attenuated top-down control of sensory cortex.

papers.title: Cardiac Arrest After Deceased Donor Kidney Transplant.
papers.abstract: A 54-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease and a dual-chamber pacemaker for high-grade atrioventricular block underwent deceased donor kidney transplantation. Her postoperative course was complicated by marked QT prolongation and recurrent torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Postarrest electrocardiogram demonstrated macroscopic T-wave alternans-a rare manifestation of severe QT prolongation. Treatment with intravenous magnesium and reprogramming her pacemaker to a lower rate limit of 100 beats/min resulted in electrical stability and improvement of the QT interval. This case underscores recognition of macroscopic T-wave alternans as a harbinger of impending TdP, vigilant QT monitoring, and evidence-based TdP management.

papers.title: Susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors in relation to visual working memory in children with and without attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder associated with increased distractibility. Previous research has reported that susceptibility to task-irrelevant visual distraction is linked with visual working memory (WM) capacity in adults. Here, we examined how neural susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors related to visual WM capacity in children with and without ADHD. Across two experiments, electroencephalography (EEG) signals were recorded from 146 Chinese children aged 7-15 (63 with ADHD, 23% girls; collected in 2022-2024), during which they performed visual tasks of varying difficulty with auditory distractors. The mismatch negativity (MMN) amplitude was measured as neural susceptibility to auditory distractors, and a K-score was calculated to assess visual WM capacity. In typically developing (TD) children, those with higher visual WM capacity showed less susceptibility to auditory distractors under high audiovisual competition (r = 0.494), whereas this relation reversed under low competition (r = -0.319). Conversely, in children with ADHD, lower visual WM capacity predicted higher susceptibility under both high (r = 0.442) and low competition (r = 0.326). These findings indicate that susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distraction is related to visual WM capacity in children, but the patterns differ between typical and atypical neurodevelopment and are modulated by audiovisual competition.

papers.title: Individualized intraoperative BIS targeting based on preoperative BIS values in the awake state: a review and strategy prospect for preventing postoperative delirium in older patients.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication in older surgical patients and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is widely used to guide intraoperative depth of anesthesia. However, the conventional strategy of maintaining a uniform BIS target range may not adequately account for interindividual differences in preoperative brain function, particularly in older adults with reduced neural reserve. This narrative review integrates evidence from three complementary domains: 1) clinical studies evaluating the association between preoperative resting BIS values in the awake state and the risk of POD; 2) mechanistic and clinical evidence linking excessive anesthetic depth, particularly electroencephalographic burst suppression, to POD; 3) interventional trials assessing the effect of intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia management on delirium outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that a lower preoperative resting BIS value in the awake state is potentially independently associated with an increased risk of POD in older patients. Intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia has been shown to reduce exposure to deep anesthesia and EEG burst suppression, which are consistently linked to higher delirium incidence. These findings suggest that patients with preoperatively identified brain vulnerability may benefit from higher individualized intraoperative BIS targets, rather than a fixed universal range. Integrating preoperative resting BIS assessment into perioperative anesthesia management may enable risk stratification and support individualized regulation of anesthetic depth in older adults. When incorporated into a multimodal delirium prevention framework, this individualized approach may offer a rational pathway toward improved delirium prevention and perioperative neuroprotection in older adults, warranting validation in future prospective randomized studies.

papers.title: Evidence From Disruption to Therapy: A Systematic Review of Lighting Interventions for Night Shift Nurses.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of lighting-based interventions and to support night-shift nurses' health and well-being. The goal is to synthesize evidence on how specific lighting parameters, including spectrum, intensity, timing, and duration, can transform nighttime light exposure from a circadian disruptor into a therapeutic intervention.BackgroundSubstantial evidence indicates that disruption of circadian rhythms by nighttime light exposure poses significant health risks to night-shift workers, particularly in healthcare settings, where lighting conditions influence both staff well-being. Increasingly, research also highlights the therapeutic potential of targeted lighting interventions to support the health and performance of this vulnerable population. As such, purposeful lighting offers an opportunity to transform light from a disruptor of circadian rhythms into a therapeutic tool for night-shift caregivers.MethodThis systematic review synthesizes findings from randomized controlled trials published between 2002 and 2025 that assessed lighting interventions for night-shift staff in healthcare environments.ResultsInterventions varied in spectrum, intensity, duration, and timing; each parameter had distinct physiological and psychological effects. Blue-enriched and full-spectrum light administered during night shifts were consistently associated with improved alertness, circadian phase alignment, and melatonin regulation. By contrast, warm-spectrum or filtered light played a protective role in maintaining melatonin levels. High-intensity and longer duration exposures tended to produce stronger effects across outcomes.ConclusionsCollectively, these findings support the adoption of evidence-based, personalized lighting strategies in healthcare design. Strategic manipulation of lighting features can improve staff well-being and performance, patient safety, and overall quality of care.

papers.title: Decoupled Adult and Larval Host Preferences in Tephritid Fruit Flies with a Conserved Oviposition Attractant.
papers.abstract: Tephritid fruit flies exhibit considerable variability in host range, yet the chemosensory mechanisms underlying adult host selection and larval performance across species with contrasting dietary breadths remain unclear. Here, we investigated behavioral responses of adults and larvae of four species─Bactrocera dorsalis, B. correcta, Zeugodacus tau, and Z. cucurbitae─to seven fruit and vegetable cues. Adult preferences varied, with guava eliciting the strongest attraction in all species. Larval preferences were weaker and decoupled from adult choices. Comparative transcriptomics of guava-exposed antennae identified OBP19d as the most highly upregulated odorant-binding protein across species. RNAi knockdown of BdOBP19d in B. dorsalis reduced electrophysiological responses to guava volatiles and specifically abolished oviposition preference for 4-Ethylacetophenone. Molecular docking, electrophysiology, and behavioral assays collectively validated this interaction. These results reveal a conserved olfactory module for shared host attraction and identify 4-Ethylacetophenone as a candidate attractant for B. dorsalis females, with potential implications for pest management.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Associations of Smartphone Use Time and Sleep Duration With Academic Performance Among Korean Adolescents by School Level.
papers.abstract: Excessive smartphone use and short sleep are common among Korean adolescents facing intense academic pressure, but few studies compare their associations with performance by school level. We analyzed data from 48,844 students from the 20th Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey (2024); multivariable regression analyses used 31,902 complete cases. Ordinal logistic regression was stratified by school level, and multinomial logistic regression with school-level interactions was conducted as a co-primary analysis. A three-category smartphone use-time variable (≤ 240, 241-480, and > 480 min/day) was examined in a sensitivity analysis. High smartphone use time (> 240 min/day) was associated with lower performance in middle school (OR = 0.47) and high school (OR = 0.65) students. Among high schoolers, shorter sleep was associated with higher odds of better performance; this pattern was absent among middle schoolers. The school level × sleep interaction was significant (p < 0.001), but the school level × use-time interaction was not. The associations of smartphone use and sleep with academic performance should be interpreted and addressed in light of both school level and the broader educational and sociocultural context, including school culture and examination-related academic pressures. Higher smartphone use time was associated with lower academic performance across both school levels, whereas the association between sleep duration and academic performance differed by school level.

papers.title: Isolation of Ventricular Cardiomyocytes from the Annual Killifish Nothobranchius furzeri for Whole-Cell Patch Clamp Recordings.
papers.abstract: Isolated working cardiomyocytes remain the standard approach for studying cardiac electrophysiology. Single-cell preparations allow for direct investigation and precise measurement of ionic currents and action potentials without the structural complexity of intact cardiac tissue. Nothobranchius furzeri (African turquoise killifish) has rapidly emerged as a prominent model organism for gerontological research due to its exceptionally short lifespan and similarities in aging mechanisms with mammals, including humans. This species combines practical advantages such as small size, inexpensive husbandry, and a rapid life cycle with translational relevance. N. furzeri exhibits age-dependent declines in locomotor activity, cognition, and organ function, accumulation of molecular hallmarks of aging, and sensitivity to pharmacological treatments that modulate lifespan and healthspan. However, investigating the functional decline of the aging heart requires a reliable method to obtain high-quality, viable cells suitable for demanding single-cell techniques. This study optimized a previously described protocol for the isolation of Danio rerio cardiomyocytes to ensure consistent recovery of healthy working myocytes from both young and senescent N. furzeri. This protocol describes the isolation of ventricular cardiomyocytes from N. furzeri specifically optimized for the whole-cell patch clamp technique. The article demonstrates how to efficiently excise the heart, perform enzymatic dissociation of the myocardium by retrograde perfusion, and store the isolated cardiomyocytes. We discuss the selection of enzymes required to digest the extracellular matrix and intercellular junctions without compromising ion channel structure. Freshly isolated cardiomyocytes are suitable for high-resolution electrophysiological assays, including action potential recordings and measurements of major inward and outward ionic currents across age groups. The article also addresses the features of cardiomyocyte isolation in fish that differ from standard mammalian isolation procedures.

papers.title: Sedative Potential of L (+)-Tartaric Acid: Behavioral Evidence With In Silico Insights Into Possible GABAergic Interaction.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent neurological disorder often caused by stress, anxiety, and imbalances in the GABAergic system. Although benzodiazepines like diazepam (DZP) are commonly prescribed, their long-term use is associated with adverse effects, including dependence and impaired coordination. Therefore, there is growing interest in natural alternatives with safer pharmacological profiles. This study aimed to investigate the sedative-like potential of L (+)-tartaric acid (LTA), a naturally occurring organic acid, through both in vivo and in silico approaches targeting the γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABAA) receptor. Sedative-like activity was evaluated in Swiss albino mice using thiopental sodium-induced sleeping time, open-field, and rotarod tests. LTA significantly reduced sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in a dose-dependent manner, with the higher dose (240 mg/kg) producing a more pronounced effect. Co-administration of LTA with DZP further enhanced thiopental-induced hypnosis. In the open-field test, LTA reduced locomotor and exploratory activities, as evidenced by decreases in square crossings, rearing, and grooming behaviors. Rotarod assessment demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in motor coordination and neuromuscular performance, although the impairment remained less pronounced than that produced by DZP at the lower tested dose. Molecular docking revealed lower binding affinity than DZP but demonstrated multiple hydrogen-bond (HB) interactions with key amino acid (AA) residues of the GABAA receptor, suggesting a potentially stable receptor interaction. Collectively, the behavioral and computational findings indicate that LTA possesses sedative-like properties and may modulate GABAergic neurotransmission. Further mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and electrophysiological studies are required to clarify its precise mode of action and therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
papers.abstract: Multisystem effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) beyond cardiometabolic outcomes are incompletely characterized against active comparators in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We compared GLP-1RA with sulfonylureas (SUs), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is) in adults with T2D. In a multicenter target trial emulation across 5 University of California academic medical centers (2012-2025) using harmonized electronic health record data, adults with T2D newly initiating GLP-1RA, SU, SGLT2i, or DPP4i were propensity score-matched 1-to-1 within site via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (>11 000 covariates), with up to 5-year follow-up. We screened 181 prespecified incident outcomes across 15 body systems, pooling hazard ratios by random-effects meta-analysis. Robustness required leave-one-medical-center-out stability, E-value ≥1.5, and false discovery rate-adjusted P < .10. Among 70 982 matched adults, 118 robust associations were identified (65 for reduced risk and 53 for increased risk). Risk reductions were most consistent for cardiovascular outcomes, including myocarditis/cardiomyopathy (summary hazard ratio, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.32-0.44] vs SGLT2i), acute myocardial infarction (0.53 [0.42-0.66]), heart failure (0.71 [0.58-0.88] vs DPP4i), and thromboembolism (0.69-0.72), and for nephritis/nephrosis (0.73 [0.67-0.79]), nutritional anemia (0.70-0.81), coagulation disorders (0.73-0.81), and tobacco-related disorders (0.60 [0.49-0.74]). Risk increases were found for musculoskeletal conditions (22 associations); osteoarthritis 1.48 (1.29-1.68), stress fractures 1.68 (1.15-2.47), diverticular disease (1.18-1.33), sleep-wake disorders (1.27-1.54), and menopausal disorders (1.32-1.52). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist initiation was associated with reduced cardiovascular, renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related risk, consistent with outcome trials. Increased risks for musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, and sleep-wake disorders warrant monitoring as the clinical use of GLP-1RAs continues to expand.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology

papers.title: Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography to Study Alterations in Biogenic Amines in Drosophila Models of Brain Disorders.
papers.abstract: Many neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders are characterized by disruptions in brain neurotransmitters, including alterations in the levels of the biogenic amines (BAs) dopamine (DA) and serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT), as well as in their release or reuptake. These neurochemical changes correlate with distinct key behavioral phenotypes, such as locomotor deficits, sleep fragmentation, and altered stress responses, among others. Because the principal BA systems interact, disease models frequently show coordinated shifts across multiple amines rather than isolated changes in a single neurotransmitter. Therefore, accurate, simultaneous quantification of several BAs is essential for interpreting behavioral and genetic findings. Drosophila melanogaster offers a genetically tractable system for modeling such disorders and neurotransmitter changes, but BAs occur in fly brain tissue at very low, nanomolar-to-femtomolar concentrations, and the small size of the Drosophila central nervous system makes their detection technically challenging. This study describes a protocol to detect and quantify DA, 5-HT, and octopamine in fly brains using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrochemical detection (HPLC-ECD). HPLC-ECD was applied to detect changes in brain DA and 5-HT in a fly model of Parkinson's disease based on dopaminergic overexpression of human alpha-synuclein. Applying this protocol to the alpha-synuclein Parkinson's disease model reveals significantly elevated dopamine, but unchanged serotonin, relative to controls, consistent with early compensatory dopaminergic mechanisms. This approach provides a sensitive, low-cost, and readily accessible method for multiplexed BA quantification from limited Drosophila tissue. It also enables systematic screening of genetic modifiers and candidate therapeutics targeting monoaminergic pathways relevant to human brain disorders.

papers.title: Non-Invasive Neuromodulation for Post-Stroke Anxiety Symptoms: An Umbrella Review and Evidence Mapping of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke anxiety can impair rehabilitation, participation, and quality of life. This umbrella review mapped systematic reviews on non-invasive neuromodulation for anxiety symptoms after stroke. PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception through June 1, 2026. Published reviews with quantitative anxiety results were eligible, including reviews in which anxiety was secondary to pain, sleep disturbance, or depression. Reporting completeness, methodological quality, and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Seven reviews were mapped, comprising six pairwise meta-analyses and one Bayesian network meta-analysis. Selected estimates suggested symptom improvement, whereas others showed no clear difference. All reviews had low or critically low methodological quality. Interpretation was limited by overlapping trials, small outcome-specific sample sizes, heterogeneous interventions, and inconsistencies across source reports. Anxiety-score changes in populations recruited for other post-stroke conditions do not establish a direct effect on clinically defined post-stroke anxiety. Source-level population eligibility and certainty judgments require particular scrutiny when mixed neurological populations contribute to pooled estimates. Non-invasive neuromodulation remains investigational for post-stroke anxiety. Current evidence does not support routine use of a specific protocol or replacement of standard multidisciplinary stroke care. Future trials should prospectively define anxiety, standardize stimulation and sham procedures, and assess sustained benefit and safety.

papers.title: Neuromelanin-Sensitive MRI as a Marker of Clinical Severity and Disease Burden in Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The neuropathology of Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized in part by the degeneration of catecholaminergic neurons, particularly dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus (LC), yet no validated in vivo biomarker quantifies this process. Neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging (NM-MRI) enables noninvasive assessment of these neuronal populations, although relationships with clinical severity, disease burden, and progression remain incompletely defined. We conducted the first Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis examining associations between NM-MRI measures and clinical outcomes in PD, including subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Reduced NM-MRI measures were associated with greater motor impairment (18 studies; pooled r = -0.406), longer disease duration (14; r = -0.426), higher Hoehn and Yahr stage (10; r = -0.336), and higher levodopa equivalent daily dose (6; r = -0.337) (all P < 0.001). Thirty-nine studies (1983 patients with PD) were included in the systematic review. Narrative synthesis demonstrated distinct SNpc/LC associations: SNpc measures were primarily associated with motor dysfunction and disease stage, displaying hemispheric asymmetry, intranigral topography, and phenotype-specific patterns, whereas LC measures were preferentially linked to cognitive, affective, autonomic, and sleep-related symptoms. Four longitudinal studies (~1.5-3 years) reported declines in selected NM-MRI measures (~5%-19% annually). Multimodal studies suggested NM-MRI captures a complementary dimension of nigrostriatal pathology alongside dopaminergic, iron-sensitive, and diffusion-based markers. NM-MRI provides a biologically interpretable in vivo measure of catecholaminergic neuron integrity and survival in PD, with consistent cross-sectional associations with clinical disease burden. Emerging longitudinal and multimodal evidence supports its potential as a progression-sensitive imaging biomarker for disease-modifying clinical trials. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Risk Factors for Cardiovascular Mortality in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, but the relative contributions of OSA-specific parameters versus classical cardiometabolic risk factors remain poorly defined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,368 consecutive adults referred for diagnostic polysomnography at a tertiary sleep center and followed for up to 20 years. The primary outcome was cause-specific cardiovascular mortality ascertained by national death registry linkage. Analyses integrated cause-specific Cox regression, Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, and a random survival forest (RSF) competing-risk model (1000 trees; 70/30 train-test split). Gower-distance-based hierarchical clustering of RSF-predicted cumulative incidence identified patient phenotypes. Over a median follow-up of 8.6 years (interquartile range 6.7-12.5), 335 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Heart failure (30.4%), chronic ischemic heart disease (14.0%), and acute myocardial infarction (11.6%) were the leading causes. Independent predictors were age (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.10, per year), male sex (1.68, 1.29-2.18), active smoking (1.68, 1.30-2.15), hypertension (1.73, 1.29-2.33), atrial fibrillation (2.16, 1.56-2.98), prior myocardial infarction (1.71, 1.25-2.35), and diabetes (1.37, 1.06-1.76). Nocturnal desaturation lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Among patients with an apnea-hypopnea index ≥15 events/h, a good continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) response was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (0.72, 0.55-0.96). The RSF C-index was 0.80. Six phenotypes showed cardiovascular mortality of 2.9% to 14.4%. Cardiovascular mortality in OSA was driven predominantly by classical cardiometabolic risk factors rather than by nocturnal hypoxemic burden or CPAP response. Comorbidity-targeted prevention should be prioritized, and phenotype-aware stratification may identify subgroups warranting intensified cardiovascular surveillance.

papers.title: No significant change in urinary sodium excretion within 48h after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery: the weight LUSER study.
papers.abstract: Metabolic and bariatric surgery is effective in achieving remission of hypertension and metabolic disease. It is unclear whether metabolic changes within the first 48h after surgery can potentially explain underlying mechanisms of hypertension control. We aimed to assess changes in urinary sodium excretion early after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) as a potential weight-loss-independent mechanism of hypertension remission. All patients undergoing primary RYGB provided a 24-h urine collection, blood pressure (BP) measurement, and blood sampling both preoperatively and 48h postoperatively. The dietary sodium content was similar at both time points. Twenty patients were included, of whom 16 met the minimum output urine volume criteria for 24-h urine samples. Mean patient age was 55.2 ± 7.7 years and median body mass index was 48kg/m2 with 13 patients (65%) diagnosed with hypertension and 7 (35%) with obstructive sleep apnoea. Twenty-four-hour urine sodium excretion was similar immediately prior to surgery and 48h postoperatively (72.1 ± 44.0 vs 74.5 ± 65.2mmol/24h, p = 0.45). There was no significant difference in systolic or diastolic BP immediately prior to surgery compared with 48h postoperatively (143.3 ± 15.1 vs 135.9 ± 16.3mmHg, p = 0.09 and 79.8 ± 9.2 vs 79.9 ± 5.8mmHg, p = 0.47). Both findings were confirmed on further sensitivity analysis. No significant change in urinary sodium excretion or BP was detected in the first 48h post RYGB in normotensive patients or those with well-controlled hypertension.
papers.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

papers.title: Enhancing Sleep in NCAA Division I Athletes: A Study of Sleep Extension Feasibility.
papers.abstract: Sleep extension has been shown to improve varied aspects of athletic performance in collegiate athletes. Such studies have been conducted in small cohorts in controlled settings utilizing obsolete monitoring technology. The feasibility of sleep extension has not been evaluated in a broader cohort of collegiate athletes with modern monitoring technology. Sleep extension may not be feasible in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I athletes. Crossover study. Level 3. Baseline sleep data were collected from NCAA Division I athletes (women's soccer, men's soccer, baseball, and football) during a 2-week period. Subjects were then instructed to extend their total sleep time to 10 hours per night for 2 weeks. All sleep baseline and extension data were collected in the offseason, remote from school examinations. WHOOP bands recorded all sleep metrics. Data were analyzed using paired-samples t tests and Wilcoxon signed rank tests. A total of 50 subjects (14 female, 36 male) participated. The study compared total sleep time (hours) and sleep consistency (percent) - the stability of sleep-wake schedule over time, between baseline and sleep extension phases. Sample size varied for both metrics, ranging from 46 to 49 participants, respectively. There was a statistically significant increase in sleep consistency during the sleep extension phase (baseline, 60.09 ± 12.6%; extension, 64.42 ± 12.4%; P = 0.02). However, total sleep time showed no significant difference between the 2 phases (baseline, 7.63 ± 0.88 hours; extension, 7.51 ± 0.88 hours; P = 0.27). Extension efforts improved sleep consistency but did not significantly impact total sleep time suggesting that a sleep extension intervention can enhance sleep consistency in NCAA Division I athletes but does not significantly impact total sleep time. Sleep extension may be challenging for collegiate athletes given the time-intensive demands of both academics and sports. While sleep extension may be feasible in professional sports, it does not appear to be so in the college setting. While the sleep extension intervention improved sleep consistency, it did not improve total sleep time, questioning the feasibility of sleep extension in collegiate sports.

papers.title: Dietary Inflammatory Index and Sleep Quality Among Women with Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common among women with breast cancer (BC). Recent evidence suggests that dietary inflammation may influence sleep quality, yet this association remains underexplored in BC populations. In this cross-sectional study, 600 women aged 18-75 years with pathologically confirmed BC were recruited from the Isfahan Breast Cancer Registry between 2021 and 2023. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 168-item Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and energy-adjusted DII (E-DII) scores were calculated based on 35 dietary components. Sleep quality was assessed using the validated Persian version of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI-P). A multiple linear regression model was employed to estimate adjusted regression coefficients. Higher DII and E-DII scores were significantly associated with poorer sleep quality. Each one-unit increase in DII and E-DII corresponded to a 0.34-point (95% CI: 0.11-0.57; p = 0.004) and a 0.34-point (95% CI: 0.14-0.53; p = 0.001) increase in PSQI score, respectively. A significant linear trend was observed across quartiles of DII and E-DII. Higher dietary inflammatory potential was associated with poorer sleep quality among women with BC. Considering the limitations of the cross-sectional design, longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to determine whether reducing dietary inflammatory potential can improve sleep outcomes in this population.

papers.title: Environmental and psychosocial factors in hypertension: an emerging landscape of cardiovascular risk.
papers.abstract: Environmental and psychosocial factors are increasingly recognised as important contributors to the development, progression, and control of hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular (CV) disease. Within the exposome framework, these exposures converge on shared neuroendocrine, oxidative, and inflammatory pathways leading to endothelial dysfunction and blood pressure (BP) elevation. Among environmental pollutants, air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), is a major modifiable risk factor; each 10 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 is associated with a 4% rise in HTN prevalence. Transportation noise increases HTN risk through stress-related neurohormonal activation, oxidative stress, and sleep disruption. Artificial light at night and heavy metals are additional contributors, whereas micro- and nanoplastics remain an emerging concern awaiting robust human data. Physical and climatic stressors also influence BP regulation. Both heat and cold are associated with increased CV morbidity and mortality, with cold exerting the greater impact, and hypobaric hypoxia at high altitude activates sympathetic and neurohormonal pathways that promote BP elevation, particularly in hypertensive individuals. Among psychosocial and behavioural factors, sleep disturbances are associated with incident and resistant HTN. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is an underrecognized determinant of HTN, especially among refugees, migrants, war veterans, and other trauma-exposed populations, through chronic sympathetic activation, inflammation, and adverse behavioural pathways. Finally, spaceflight provides a unique model of extreme environmental stress, inducing CV adaptations ranging from transient BP dysregulation and orthostatic intolerance to vascular remodelling resembling accelerated CV ageing. Recognising these determinants is essential to improve HTN prevention, optimise BP control, and reduce long-term CV risk.

papers.title: [Therapeutic play in pediatric hospitalization: a comprehensive care strategy beyond pain management].
papers.abstract: During pediatric hospitalization, invasive and painful procedures are frequently performed and may cause anxiety and fear, particularly among children who, due to their age, may not fully understand the situation. If pain is not adequately managed, it may be associated with negative consequences, such as sleep disturbances, needle phobia, and reluctance or refusal to seek or receive healthcare. Therefore, alleviating pediatric pain is both a right and a responsibility of healthcare institutions, which should implement effective pain management strategies. Among these strategies, non-pharmacological distraction is an intervention used to reduce pain and distress associated with certain procedures. It may include sensory stimuli adapted to the child's age and developmental level. In this context, play has gained relevance as a therapeutic tool, although its effects should be interpreted considering the type of intervention, the clinical context, and the quality of the available evidence. Play promotes children's emotional, cognitive, and social development and may improve their relationship with healthcare professionals and facilitate cooperation during treatment. Therefore, its incorporation from the time of hospital admission has been proposed, supported by specific institutional policies and professional training programs. Hospitals should also be provided with appropriate resources, and interdisciplinary collaboration should be promoted to ensure its effective implementation as a complementary therapeutic tool. From a public health perspective, its systematic integration should also consider equity in access, differences in resources between healthcare settings, professional training, and outcome evaluation.

papers.title: Magnetoencephalography in Parkinson's disease: diagnostic potential and barriers to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder with motor and nonmotor manifestations. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, and validated markers of early disease and subsequent progression are still needed. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures neuronal magnetic fields with millisecond temporal resolution and provides a means of characterizing cortical dysfunction. This narrative review critically synthesizes MEG evidence on periodic and aperiodic spectral activity, functional connectivity, network topology, and individual brain fingerprinting, with emphasis on diagnostic relevance and barriers to clinical translation. Recurring findings include spectral slowing and cognitive-network disruption, whereas resting β power, burst dynamics, and coupling depend on clinical phenotype, treatment state, and analytical choices. Evidence from electroencephalogram (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and invasive recordings is distinguished from direct MEG findings. Internally validated classification of established PD and healthy controls is promising, but does not establish performance in prodromal disease or clinically uncertain parkinsonism. Optically pumped magnetometers may improve recording flexibility while retaining requirements for environmental interference control. Prospective clinical cohorts, standardized acquisition and analysis, reproducibility studies, independent validation, and comparison with clinical assessment are needed to establish incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility.

papers.title: Morning affect, eveningness, and distinctness in relation to mental health-related outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies using the Morningness-Eveningness-Stability Scale improved (MESSi).
papers.abstract: Traditionally, chronotype has been conceptualized within a single morningness-eveningness continuum. However, emerging evidence suggests that a multidimensional approach may better reflect circadian functioning. This review aimed to examine the associations between chronotype characteristics derived from the leading multidimensional model, as measured by the Morningness-Eveningness-Stability Scale improved, and mental health-related outcomes in adults. A systematic search was conducted across four databases. Of 151 screened records, 20 studies comprising 11 681 adult participants met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis. Pearson's correlations were used as effect sizes, and random-effects models were applied for the meta-analysis. The three dimensions of chronotype showed distinct patterns of association with mental health-related outcomes. Morning affect (MA) was associated with lower levels of ill-being and higher levels of well-being, whereas Distinctness (DI) showed the opposite pattern. Within the available MESSi literature, Eveningness (EV) showed weaker and less consistent associations with the examined outcomes than MA and DI. Meta-analytic findings indicated that MA and DI were more strongly and consistently associated with the examined mental health-related outcomes than EV. Overall, these findings support a multidimensional conceptualization of chronotype and suggest that aspects of circadian functioning beyond eveningness may be important for understanding individual differences in mental health-related outcomes.

papers.title: Together we "CAM": 12 open questions in Crassulacean acid metabolism biology.
papers.abstract: Crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) is a remarkable example of convergent evolution and is a versatile photosynthetic adaptation across the tree of life. It often receives less research attention than C3 or C4 photosynthesis, but as the consequences of climate change become more drastic, research into bioengineering CAM has become increasingly timely for its adaptive advantage during drought. Regardless of a biotechnological application, several aspects of CAM biology are still poorly understood. Here, we highlight 12 questions that have the potential to advance the field of CAM biology, covering a wide range of topics, from mechanistic, physiological, evolutionary to applied themes, including stomatal kinetics, vacuolar malate transport, mitochondrial respiration, the circadian clock, phenotypic definitions, sensing stress to induce CAM, ecophysiological significance of CAM, phytohormone signaling, multi-level molecular regulation, genetic engineering, climate change, and evolution of CAM. Overall, we also highlight the ultimate need for exploring the numerous CAM phenotypes instead of only model species. This perspective article provides a broad yet detailed overview of CAM biology and aims to inspire more work in the field. We aimed to highlight key knowledge gaps and future research opportunities, thereby underscoring the timely significance and relevance of CAM.

papers.title: A re-tightening suture technique for hemostasis during aortic root remodeling in chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection.
papers.abstract: We report a 45-year-old man with chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection, a sinus of Valsalva aneurysm, and severe aortic regurgitation. His atopic dermatitis remained poorly controlled despite topical corticosteroids and injectable anti-inflammatory therapy and he occasionally experienced cutaneous bleeding from unconscious scratching during sleep. He therefore wished to avoid long-term anticoagulation. Valve-sparing root replacement using root remodeling with external annuloplasty was performed. Bleeding from the proximal continuous suture line was controlled using a re-tightening suture technique that lifted the bleeding point, facilitated placement of an additional mattress suture, and secured the redundant continuous suture under renewed tension. Postoperative imaging showed satisfactory root geometry and no residual aortic regurgitation. This technique may provide a simple and reproducible method for controlling difficult suture-line bleeding during root remodeling.

papers.title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women. This triple-blind randomised controlled trial study was conducted in August to November 2023 with eligible primiparous women who gave birth at Health Centers No. 2 and 3, Mashhad, Iran. The participants were randomly and equally divided into two groups: (1) the probiotic group, which received probiotic capsules (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus, Bifidobacterium bifidum, B. lactis and B. longum) and (2) the placebo group, which received placebo capsules. All participants received one capsule daily from the third day after delivery for 30 days. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire was completed before and after the study. Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests, T-test and Mann-Whitney test were used for statistical analysis. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. A total of 60 women were included in this study (n = 30 for each group). The two groups were homogeneous in terms of demographic and obstetric characteristics except for body mass index. Before the intervention, the overall score of postpartum quality of sleep in the probiotic and placebo groups was 9.66 ± 6.21 and 11.70 ± 6.68, respectively; after the intervention, the probiotic group had a score of 6.16 ± 2.75 with the score difference of -3.50 ± 5.53 and the placebo group a score of 6.60 ± 2.66 with the score difference of -5.10 ± 6.31 with a statistically significant difference in the intervention group compared to the placebo (P = 0.003). Consumption of probiotic capsules improves the quality of sleep and maternal health in the postpartum period.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of YZG-331 ameliorated insomnia based on the gut microbiota-drug interaction.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in the study of drug efficacy and metabolism. YZG-331 exhibits significant sedative and hypnotic effects. However, the oral bioavailability of YZG-331 in female mice remains low at 27.7%, and it exhibits instability in the gut microbiota, undergoing rapid metabolism, with the intestinal hydrolytic metabolite M2 identified as the characteristic metabolite. Both the underlying mechanisms of YZG-331 therapeutic effects on insomnia and its enzyme-mediated metabolic pathways involving the gut microbiota remain incompletely elucidated. In this study, we found that YZG-331 regulated the tryptophan metabolism and 5-HT production pathways by the gut microbiota. Specifically, YZG-331 increased the abundance of Lactobacillus and Muribaculaceae in the gut, with Lactobacillus reuteri playing a critical role in both the metabolic processes of YZG-331 and the biosynthesis of tryptophan-derived metabolites. YZG-331 enhanced the activation of the tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) cofactor system, which subsequently promoted tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) activity, thereby enhancing 5-HT production. Furthermore, YZG-331 and M2 increased intestinal butyric acid levels, thereby promoting sleep regulation and supporting the restoration of the intestinal barrier. Overall, our study provided the first evidence highlighting the crucial role of the gut microbiota in the therapeutic mechanism and metabolic processing of YZG-331 in the treatment of insomnia.

papers.title: Association Between Uncertainty Stress and Insomnia Symptoms Among Chinese Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: The Mediating Role of Healthy Lifestyles Based on a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore the association between uncertainty stress and insomnia symptoms and further examine the mediating mediating association of verify the mediating role of healthy lifestyles among Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted based on 3361 patients with type 2 diabetes recruited from 26 community health service centers across China from November 2023 to March 2024. Pearson's correlation test was applied to explore the relationships among the key variables. Regression models were used to examine the mediating associations of healthy Lifestyles. Moreover, Sobel's test and the bootstrap method were employed to confirm the path effects in the models, ensuring the reliability and validity of the results. Out of 3361 diabetes patients, participants had a mean age of 62.16 years, and 51.35% were male. 30.08% experienced insomnia. There was a significant correlation between uncertainty stress, healthy lifestyles, and Insomnia Symptoms (p < 0.01). Uncertainty stress was positively associated with Insomnia Symptoms (β = 0.49, p < 0.01) and negatively associated with on healthy lifestyles (β = - 0.02, p < 0.01). Healthy Lifestyles were negatively associated with insomnia symptoms (β = -0.62, p < 0.001). A small exploratory indirect association of uncertainty stress with insomnia symptoms through healthy lifestyles was observed (β = 0.015, p < 0.001). The Sobel and bootstrap tests confirmed the robustness of the regression analyses. Uncertainty stress was positively associated with insomnia symptoms in patients with type 2 diabetes, and healthy lifestyles may partially mediate this association. These findings suggest that reducing uncertainty stress and promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors may be promising targets for future interventions to improve sleep health among community-dwelling adults with type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Integration of Aromatherapy and Essential Oils in Asthma Symptom Relief: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Asthma affects 262 million people globally, causing 455,000 preventable deaths, with higher mortality in low-resource areas due to limited diagnosis and treatment. Aromatherapy, using bioactive essential oils (EOs), has emerged as a promising complementary approach for asthma symptom management. This review synthesizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of EOs in alleviating asthma-related inflammation, bronchoconstriction, and immune dysregulation through anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and immunomodulatory mechanisms. Key oils such as lavender, eucalyptus, and peppermint demonstrate efficacy in reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, oxidative stress, and Th2-mediated inflammation, supported by preclinical and clinical studies. Methods of application, including inhalation, topical use, and environmental diffusion, are evaluated for their physiological and psychological benefits, particularly in stress and sleep modulation, which are critical to asthma control. Safety considerations, such as allergenicity, proper dosing, and potential drug interactions, are emphasized to ensure safe integration with conventional therapies. Despite the promising findings, further large-scale clinical trials are needed to validate the efficacy, optimize protocols, and explore personalized approaches based on genetic and phenotypic variability. This review underscores aromatherapy's role as an adjunctive therapy within a holistic asthma management framework, bridging traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific validation to improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: A Comparative Review of Performance and Concurrent Cardiac Rhythm Assessment Across Home Sleep Apnea Testing Devices.
papers.abstract: Home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) is now widely used in place of in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) for the evaluation of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), but published performance varies across FDA-cleared devices. This narrative review aimed to summarize the published performance of FDA-cleared Type III HSAT devices currently marketed in the United States and compare their labeled capabilities for assessing SDB over multiple nights and concurrently evaluating cardiac rhythm and atrial fibrillation (AF) burden. A search of the FDA 510(k) database identified 68 devices with MNR as the primary product code that were cleared after August 1, 2016, or were cleared earlier but released for sale after that date. There were 13 devices that met these criteria and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) criteria for a Type III HSAT. For each device, sensitivity and specificity against PSG, scored under American Academy of Sleep Medicine Rule 1B (4% oxygen desaturation), were obtained from the FDA 510(k) Summary or a peer-reviewed validation study. Balanced accuracy (the mean of sensitivity and specificity) was calculated at apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds of 5, 15, and 30 events per hour. Five devices were excluded from the comparison and are reported for information only because their performance data were not reported using a methodology consistent with that of the other devices: they used a different scoring rule or severity threshold, reported central apnea detection only, or relied on a less credible source for the reported data. Among the remaining eight devices, reported sample sizes ranged from 30 to 476 subjects. All eight reported performance at AHI ≥ 15, five at AHI ≥ 5, and three at AHI ≥ 30. At AHI ≥ 15, balanced accuracy was highest for AcuPebble Ox200 (Acurable Limited, London, UK) (96.5), followed by WatchPAT SW (Itamar Medical, Caesarea, Israel) (94.0) and RX-1 Sleep (Rhythm Express, St. Paul, MN) (92.2). RX-1 Sleep reported the highest balanced accuracy at AHI ≥ 5 (90.9) and AHI ≥ 30 (92.9). These comparisons are indirect and descriptive: each device was validated against PSG in a separate cohort, none was evaluated against another device in the same patients, and between-device differences were not statistically tested. Prospective head-to-head studies against a common reference standard would be needed to confirm differences in relative performance. Among the devices compared, RX-1 Sleep system provides an aid for concurrent assessment of SDB and AF burden in a single test. Other devices can flag or record rhythm information but cannot quantify AF burden. Together with its published performance and multi-night testing capability, this may offer clinical benefit given the severity-dependent association between SDB and AF burden and the elevated cardiovascular risk observed when the two conditions coexist.

papers.title: Building a Sustainable Teen Wellness Curriculum in a Faith-Based Community Setting : A Six-Year Program Evaluation in Wilmington, Delaware.
papers.abstract: In the United States, the need for adolescent mental health support is greater than what clinical services can provide, with about one in five teens reporting unmet needs. Faith-based organizations are trusted and easy to access, but evidence on sustained delivery is limited. This report looks at a volunteer-led teen wellness program at Manna House Fellowship in Wilmington, Delaware, which ran from June 2020 to July 2026. The program offered 30-minute interactive small-group sessions every two weeks during active cycles, focusing on sleep, nutrition, physical activity, screen and social media use, and stress coping. Sessions were held online until March 2022, then in person. Over six years, 78 sessions reached 35 different teens, averaging eight participants per session, with most attending more than once. Anonymous feedback was collected monthly in written and verbal formats, and reported changes were noted. No one needed to be referred to formal mental health services. That the program has continued for six years without outside funding or paid staff support the feasibility of this sustained community wellness program, although not its clinical effectiveness. Zero recorded referrals do not establish an absence of unmet mental health needs.

papers.title: Altered network organization with shift to local processing during adaptive behaviour in multiple sclerosis.
papers.abstract: To adjust to changing environmental demands, the brain needs to organize and (re)configure mental resources in so-called task sets. Following a network perspective of cognitive functions, these processes are considered to rely on dynamic exchange of information between distant brain regions, possibly synchronized by slow-wave theta oscillations. However, few attempts have been made to describe the directional transfer of information in theta networks during behavioural adaptation. In the current study, we examined directed neural information transfer in 57 healthy individuals and 57 patients with multiple sclerosis with a focus on brain-behaviour associations during task switching. For this, we calculated behavioural switch costs and further applied an artificial neural network-based approach on neurophysiological EEG data to estimate linear and non-linear effective connectivity measures within cortical networks during task switching. Source reconstruction and connectivity analyses revealed distinct neural network architectures and communication strategies during task switching in healthy controls compared to patients with multiple sclerosis. In healthy controls, enhanced modulations of long-range fronto-parietal connectivities were associated with higher reaction time switch costs, possibly reflecting increased cognitive demands rather than adaptive processes. In contrast, patients with multiple sclerosis relied more strongly on local intra-regional modulations, which is consistent with the idea of a dysconnectivity syndrome in multiple sclerosis. Strikingly, stronger modulations in self-connectivities were associated with better accuracy measures in patients with multiple sclerosis, suggesting a compensatory mechanism to support performance. Notably, only non-linear directed connectivity measures were related to behavioural switch costs, emphasizing the importance of non-linear models for adaptive cognitive processes.

papers.title: The Association Between Sleep and Obesity in Adults: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses.
papers.abstract: Short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, and circadian disruption have been linked to obesity, but the proliferation of systematic reviews with meta-analyses (SRMAs) has fragmented the evidence. No prior umbrella review has synthesized all sleep characteristics exclusively in adults or formally graded the credibility of associations. We aimed to evaluate the association between various sleep characteristics and obesity‑related outcomes in adults. We conducted an umbrella review of SRMAs. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Scopus, CINAHL, and Epistemonikos were searched from inception to March 1, 2026. We included SRMAs examining adults (≥ 18 years) reporting any sleep exposure and obesity outcomes. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. Overlap of primary studies was quantified with the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence was graded using Ioannidis criteria. Sixteen SRMAs encompassing approximately 13.8 million participants were included. Primary study overlap was very low (overall CCA = 0.024). Short sleep duration was associated with a 40% increased odds of obesity (pooled OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.27-1.55; I2 = 83.7%). Long sleep showed a modest association (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08; I2 = 0%). Both were classified as Class III (Suggestive) evidence. Daytime napping, social jetlag, and insomnia symptoms met only Class IV (Weak) criteria. Objective sleep measurement (polysomnography) yielded substantially larger effects (OR 2.70, 95% CI 1.80-4.05) than self‑report (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.98-1.33). AMSTAR 2 assessment revealed two high‑quality, four moderate, nine low, and one critically low review. Short and long sleep durations are suggestively associated with obesity in adults, with short sleep showing a stronger effect. Other sleep characteristics have weak or limited evidence. Clinicians should consider sleep duration a potentially modifiable risk factor for obesity. CRD420261326462.

papers.title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure. To perform a systematic and comprehensive bibliometric analysis of cDMRI to explore current status, research hotspots and potential future directions. A systematic search of Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and PubMed was conducted to identify articles on cDMRI published between 2005 and 2024. All retrieved records were independently screened by two reviewers to exclude the articles unrelated to the topic about cDMRI. Co-citation, collaboration networks, burst keywords, and reference analyses were performed. There were 359 articles searched in WoSCC and 88 articles in PubMed. Finally, 367 articles met the search criteria in both databases. The cardiac "diffusion tensor imaging" (cDTI) emerged as the most prominent keyword, with the highest occurrence count (191.0) and strongest citation bursts (6.8). The study by Nielles-Vallespin et al. showed the strongest citation burst (26.17), accumulating 163 total citations and an average of 20.38 citations per year, highlighting its substantial influence on the development of cDMRI research. The top-cited articles with the strongest citation bursts concentrated on the clinical application of cDTI, its sequence design, and cardiac electrophysiology based on cDTI. The trend topic analysis further revealed "deep learning" as an emerging research focus in cDMRI since 2022. To our knowledge, this is the first dedicated bibliometric analysis focusing on cDMRI. By systematically analyzing the current status, research hotspots, and future trends of cDMRI, it provided valuable insights to guide future investigations in this field.

papers.title: Non-linear association between average daily sleep duration and cardiovascular disease in patients with diabetes or prediabetes.
papers.abstract: The relationship between sleep duration and cardiovascular disease (CVD) has garnered increasing attention, yet its specific shape and quantitative characteristics remain poorly defined in populations with disordered glucose metabolism-namely diabetes and prediabetes-who face substantially elevated cardiovascular risk. This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-2020. The study population comprised 7,835 participants with diabetes or prediabetes. Logistic regression was applied to adjust for demographic, behavioural, and metabolic confounders. Smooth curve fitting and segmented threshold effect analyses were further employed to characterise the dose-response relationship in detail. Compared with the reference sleep duration of 7-9 h/day, both short (< 7 h) and long (≥ 9 h) sleep were independently associated with significantly higher odds of CVD, with fully adjusted odds ratios of 1.27 (95% CI: 1.03-1.56, P = 0.024) and 1.37 (95% CI: 1.11-1.69, P = 0.004), respectively. A significant non-linear relationship with a clear threshold was identified, with an inflection point at 8.36 h/day. Below this threshold, each one-hour increase in sleep was associated with an 11% reduction in CVD risk (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.83-0.96, P = 0.004); above it, each additional hour corresponded to a 27% higher risk (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.13-1.42, P < 0.001). This non-linear threshold effect was consistently observed across secondary outcomes, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, and stroke. This study reveals a non-linear association between daily sleep duration and CVD risk in patients with diabetes or prediabetes. Both insufficient and excessive sleep are associated with an increased CVD odds, indicating a nonlinear pattern. Further research is warranted to delve into the causal mechanisms. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02120-1.

papers.title: Dynamic bio-psychologic profiles: Tracking burnout and recovery in surgical trainees.
papers.abstract: Burnout affects 67% to 95% of surgical trainees and attrition approaches 3% per year, making both among the highest rates across all specialties. The discrepancy between burnout and attrition suggests potential reversibility and common strengths that foster retention. Most burnout studies utilize variable-centered analyses that average individuals' trajectories obscuring distinct patterns of burnout and recovery. The lack of granularity hinders identification of interventions that address specific needs of individuals. This work explored physiologic markers of stress and burnout in surgical trainees to generate bio-psychologic profiles and potential profile-specific targets for intervention. Physiologic markers, program characteristics, and burnout assessments were obtained from surgical residents over a 3-month period. Correlations, linear mixed models, and unsupervised clustering were used to explore the relationships among these variables. We evaluated 1470 nights of sleep and 179 burnout assessments across 29 surgical residents. On average, subjects contributed 56 (interquartile range, 38-71) nights of sleep and 6 (interquartile range, 5-7) burnout assessments. High levels of emotional exhaustion and depersonalization were reported in 41.3% and 39.7% of surveys, respectively, and low levels of personal accomplishment in 41.9%. Greater bedtime variability over the prior 7 days was associated with lower personal accomplishment (P = .004) and was more pronounced earlier in training (P = .001). Trainees clustered into 6 hypothesized profiles with an average of 1.05 transitions between profiles per person. Longitudinal bio-psychologic profiling in surgical trainees is feasible. Residents appear to transition between profiles, suggesting that targeted interventions tailored to profile-specific drivers warrant validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Comprehensive management of chronic insomnia in Spain: a multidisciplinary modified RAND/UCLA consensus with recommendations on daridorexant.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia is a prevalent 24-hour disorder with significant daytime impact. Its management is frequently complicated by conceptual barriers, limited use of standardised diagnostic tools and prolonged benzodiazepine use, while insomnia is often overlooked or inadequately coded as an independent disorder. These challenges highlight the need for improved recognition and clearer therapeutic pathways. Dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs), particularly daridorexant, offer a new pharmacological option targeting wake-promoting pathways, yet practical guidance on their clinical use remains limited. A multidisciplinary panel of seven experts conducted a national consensus using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Seventy-four statements addressing the nature, diagnosis and treatment of chronic insomnia, including the clinical use of daridorexant, were evaluated across two rating rounds and a structured discussion. Consensus was reached on 36 statements in round one; one statement was removed; and the remaining 37 achieved consensus in round two. Experts agreed that chronic insomnia is a distinct disorder, with hyperarousal as a central mechanism, and emphasised the importance of targeting daytime functioning and preserving sleep architecture. Daridorexant was considered appropriate across heterogeneous clinical profiles, supported by evidence demonstrating improvements in nocturnal sleep, daytime functioning and sleep architecture, along with favourable tolerability and low abuse potential. This consensus supports a pragmatic and patient-centred approach to chronic insomnia management, integrating current evidence with expert clinical experience. The recommendations may help guide decision-making in routine practice, including the use of daridorexant when pharmacological treatment is considered appropriate.

papers.title: Relationships among heart rate variability, sleep disturbances, and fatigue in patients undergoing interventional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Fatigue and sleep disturbances are commonly experienced by patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the potential association between these conditions and autonomic nervous system reflected by heart rate variability (HRV) is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the differences in HRV parameters among HCC patients with different degrees of fatigue and sleep disturbances, as well as the relationship between HRV parameters and fatigue and sleep disturbances. In this cross-sectional study, a total of 66 patients with HCC hospitalized for interventional therapy were enrolled. Patients completed questionnaires during hospitalization, including the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Fatigue Scale-14 (FS-14), and underwent a 5-minute resting electrocardiogram (ECG) for HRV analysis. Group comparisons and logistic regression models adjusted for age were used to examine the associations between HRV parameters and symptom severity, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. Acceleration capacity (AC) was significantly higher and low frequency (LF) was significantly lower in the high PSQI group compared to the low PSQI group (AC: p = 0.036; LF: p = 0.041); Compared to the low FS-14 group, the high FS-14 group had significantly higher mean heart rate (MeanHR) and AC, while most other HRV indices were significantly lower (MeanHR: p = 0.029; AC: p = 0.009). The results of the adjusted logistic regression model indicated that increased AC showed a marginal trend toward an association with poor sleep quality (p = 0.071), while MeanHR remained significantly associated with severe fatigue (OR = 1.098, p = 0.004). After FDR correction, the differences in eight HRV parameters between fatigue groups remained significant (all q < 0.05), whereas the differences between sleep-quality groups did not survive correction. Our findings suggest that alterations in HRV parameters, particularly mean heart rate (MeanHR) and acceleration capacity (AC), are associated with the severity of fatigue and sleep disturbances in HCC patients. Given the exploratory cross-sectional design, these metrics should be regarded as candidate non-invasive physiological correlates of autonomic dysfunction and symptom burden. Their clinical relevance requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200-500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1-2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal "acquisition" toward bidirectional "acquisition-modulation" closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1-2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: A bimodal deep learning framework for cerebral perfusion assessment using synchronous ECG and near-field coupled CBF signals.
papers.abstract: Accurate real-time assessment of cerebral blood flow (CBF) is crucial for optimizing treatment decisions and improving prognostic outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). In this study, leveraging the advantage of near-field coupling (NFC) technology in capturing blood flow information from intracranial vessels of different sizes, and in combination with synchronous ECG signals reflecting cardiac rhythm fluctuations, we propose a bimodal deep learning framework to characterize cerebral perfusion-related state changes under postural tilt using synchronous ECG and NFC-based CBF (NFC-CBF) signals. The framework consists of a Multi-Scale Feature Extractor (MSFE) and a Depthwise-Separable Cross-Attention Fusion (DSCAF) module, which work collaboratively to achieve hierarchical temporal representation learning and cross-modal fusion of ECG and NFC-CBF signals. Using synchronous ECG and NFC-CBF data collected from young and middle-aged healthy volunteers, we evaluated the proposed framework in binary and four-class classification tasks to assess its feasibility for cerebral perfusion-related state classification. The results show that NFC-CBF signals can capture CBF changes before and after tilt. Synchronous monitoring of ECG and NFC-CBF provided complementary information on cardiac rhythm and cerebral perfusion-related dynamics. The proposed framework outperforms Bimodal Feature Fusion, ResNet-SE-LSTM, and Cross-Transformer Network in terms of accuracy, F1-score, specificity, precision, and recall, achieving accuracies of 95.95% ± 1.54% and 79.29% ± 2.12% in the binary posture classification and four-class age-posture classification tasks, respectively. Ablation experiments indicate that bimodal modeling provided additional discriminative information compared with single-modality inputs, particularly for the four-class task involving both posture and age. The classification performance achieved after incorporating the DSCAF module is superior to that of other conventional feature fusion strategies. These findings support the feasibility of bimodal ECG and NFC-CBF modeling for cerebral perfusion-related state classification under postural perturbation, while further validation in larger, more diverse, and demographically balanced cohorts, including both patient and non-patient populations, is required before its clinical applicability can be established.

papers.title: Latent Transition Analysis of Symptom Burden Before and After Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Postoperative Lung Cancer Patients.
papers.abstract: To identify latent classes of symptom burden in lung cancer patients before and after pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) and to examine factors associated with transitions between classes. A longitudinal study. The M. D. Anderson Symptom Inventory (Chinese version) was completed by 273 postoperative lung cancer patients before (T1) and 12 weeks after PR (T2). Latent profile analysis identified symptom burden classes, and latent transition analysis estimated the probability of moving between classes. Measurement invariance was tested, and the two-class solution was retained on the basis of fit indices, entropy and interpretability. Univariate-significant variables entered a logistic regression model. Two latent classes were identified at both T1 and T2 (high and low symptom burden). The two-class solution was retained because it showed the lowest AIC, BIC and aBIC, adequate entropy (0.844 at T1; 0.902 at T2) and interpretable profiles, whereas the three-class model did not improve fit and yielded small classes. Among 262 patients (95.97% valid), the low burden class was stable (0.863), and 61.07% of patients in the high burden class at T1 moved to the low burden class at T2; these probabilities denote the proportion of patients moving between classes. Age <45 years (OR = 2.345), no financial burden (OR = 2.841), satisfactory sleep (OR = 3.130) and family living (OR = 2.949) were associated with transition from the high to the low burden class, whereas age ≥60 years (OR = 0.724), unmarried (OR = 0.418) and divorced (OR = 0.405) status with lower odds of transition. Symptom burden in postoperative lung cancer patients is heterogeneous and follows class-specific trajectories. Younger age, better sleep and stronger family and financial resources were associated with a favourable transition. As this was a single-arm observational study, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects of PR.

papers.title: Protein supplementation and resistance training-induced strength gains in young adults: a meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine whether protein supplementation confers additional benefits for muscle strength gains beyond those induced by resistance training (RT) alone in healthy young adults. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and SPORTDiscus through April 1, 2026. Twenty-three randomized controlled trials involving 611 healthy young adults were included. Pooled estimates were calculated as weighted mean differences (WMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a random-effects model. Subgroup analysis, meta-regression, and leave-one-out and leave-one-category-out sensitivity analysis were performed to explore heterogeneity. Compared with RT alone, combined RT and protein supplementation produced significant improvements in both bench press (WMD: 2.63 kg, 95% CI: 0.77-4.49, p = 0.006) and squat strength (WMD: 7.40 kg, 95% CI: 2.15-12.66, p = 0.006). Subgroup analysis revealed that the ergogenic effect on squat strength was predominantly observed when the intervention lasted ≤12 weeks, or when protein was ingested both around exercise (pre- and/or post-exercise) and before sleep. Meta-regression identified intervention duration as a significant moderator (p = 0.037) and protein timing as a borderline moderator (p = 0.073) of squat strength heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis showed that the pooled effects remained significant and consistent in direction. Protein supplementation combined with resistance training enhances muscle strength in young healthy adults, but its incremental benefit appears conditional on intervention duration, nutrient timing, training background, and baseline protein status rather than universally applicable. Future well-powered trials with standardized protein dose and source reporting, repeated measures of habitual protein intake, and stratified designs are needed to clarify these interactions and support more personalized, mechanism-informed exercise and nutrition guidance. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/# myprospero, PROSPERO, identifier: CRD42024534481.
